result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.maximal_independent_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a maximal independent set in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27095-L27198){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.maximal_independent_set( nodes=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Maximal independent set](/assets/graphs/maximal-independent-set.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A five-node graph: a triangle 2, 3, 5 with pendant nodes 1 and 4. Nodes 2 and 4, in the accent color, share no edge, and every other node is adjacent to one of them, so no node can be added. The card shows the result [2, 4], size 2, smaller than the maximum of 3." width="100%"} A maximal independent set is an independent set that cannot be extended by adding any other vertex. In other words, every vertex not in the set is adjacent to at least one vertex in the set. This uses a randomized greedy algorithm that picks nodes randomly and adds them if they don't conflict with already-chosen nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional starting set of node IDs. These nodes must already form an independent set. The algorithm will extend this set to be maximal. If `None`, starts with an empty set. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional random seed for reproducibility. If `None`, uses system entropy. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs forming a maximal independent set. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the starting nodes don't form an independent set (have adjacent nodes). [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any starting node doesn't exist in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Randomized greedy fills a set by repeatedly picking a node uniformly at random, adding it if it is not yet dominated, and removing its neighborhood from further consideration. Under a random ordering the expected running time is $O(V + E)$ with $O(V)$ auxiliary memory, and the result is guaranteed *maximal* (no further node can be added) but not necessarily *maximum*, which is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard to compute exactly. Supplying `seed=` locks reproducibility; passing `nodes=` fixes a starting independent set that the algorithm then extends. For the largest possible set, `maximum_independent_set()` runs a different (still greedy but degree-aware) heuristic. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 5-node path, a maximal independent set can pick every other node (like the two endpoints plus the middle), since no two chosen nodes are ever adjacent: ::: {#ef09c0bf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) mis = graph.maximal_independent_set(seed=23) # Verify it's actually a valid independent set graph.is_independent_set(mis) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Passing a starting node forces the algorithm to build its set around it, which is useful when you already know one node must be included: ::: {#dba6168f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) first_node = graph.get_node_ids()[0] mis = graph.maximal_independent_set(nodes=[first_node], seed=23) # Returns True: the requested starting node is always included first_node in mis ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: This scheduling-style example treats conflicting jobs as connected nodes, so a maximal independent set identifies a batch of jobs that can all run at the same time: ::: {#67ef8906 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Job_A") .add_node(label="Job_B") .add_node(label="Job_C") .add_node(label="Job_D") .add_edge("Job_A", "Job_B") # A conflicts with B .add_edge("Job_B", "Job_C") # B conflicts with C .add_edge("Job_C", "Job_D") # C conflicts with D ) parallel_jobs = graph.maximal_independent_set(seed=23) # Returns the labels of jobs that can run simultaneously [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in parallel_jobs] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['Job_A', 'Job_C'] ``` ::: :::
